microtheory.name: music_perception_cognition
microtheory.definition: How brains perceive, parse, predict, remember, emotionally respond to music. Beat induction, tonal hierarchy, expectation, emotion, memory. Where music meets brain. Major researchers: Krumhansl, Huron, Patel, Janata, Levitin, Trehub. Substrate analogue: directly maps to substrate's drive-based prediction + emotional-response mechanisms applied to music input.

concepts.name: beat_induction
concepts.definition: Listener extracts the underlying pulse from a rhythmic surface. Spontaneous; even infants do it. Large + Kolen 1994. Substrate analogue: substrate's periodicity extractor on temporal patterns.

concepts.name: metrical_structure
concepts.definition: Beats organize into stronger + weaker positions in hierarchical groups (2s, 3s, 4s). Lerdahl + Jackendoff 1983. Substrate analogue: substrate's nested temporal periodicity tracker.

concepts.name: syncopation
concepts.definition: Stress on weak beat creates tension. Resolved by return to metric alignment. Substrate analogue: substrate's expectation-violation on metric structure.

concepts.name: groove
concepts.definition: The sustained urge-to-move quality of certain rhythmic patterns. Janata 2012. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-coherence beat tracker driving motor reflex.

concepts.name: krumhansl_kessler_profile
concepts.definition: Krumhansl + Kessler 1982. Empirical key profiles: probe-tone ratings of how well each pitch class fits a key context. The tonal hierarchy. Substrate analogue: substrate's empirically-learned key-conditioned pitch distribution.

concepts.name: tonality_perception
concepts.definition: Sense that some pitches are stable + others tense within a key. Develops with exposure. Implicit cultural learning. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin landscape in pitch space.

concepts.name: key_finding
concepts.definition: Listener infers the key of a piece quickly from few pitches. Algorithm: Krumhansl-Schmuckler. Substrate analogue: substrate's pitch-distribution-to-key inference.

concepts.name: musical_expectation
concepts.definition: Listener predicts what comes next. Confirmed = pleasant; violated = surprising. Huron 2006 'Sweet Anticipation'. Substrate analogue: substrate's anticipation handler applied to music.

concepts.name: huron_itpra
concepts.definition: Huron's 5-stage emotional response: Imagination, Tension, Prediction, Reaction, Appraisal. Predicts emotional consequence of expectation. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-cascade in response to musical events.

concepts.name: tension_resolution_cycle
concepts.definition: Music creates tension (dissonance, syncopation, suspended cadences) + releases it (resolution). The cycle drives engagement. Substrate analogue: substrate's frustration buildup + resolution loop.

concepts.name: chills
concepts.definition: Goosebumps + shiver from musical climax. Dopamine release in nucleus accumbens (Salimpoor 2011). Substrate analogue: substrate's coherence-drive peak on long-anticipated resolution.

concepts.name: musical_emotion
concepts.definition: Music reliably elicits emotional responses cross-culturally. Juslin + Sloboda 2010. Mechanisms: brain stem reflex, evaluative conditioning, emotional contagion, visual imagery, episodic memory, musical expectancy. Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-mechanism affect generation from music input.

concepts.name: valence_arousal_music
concepts.definition: Music varies emotionally on valence + arousal axes. Russell. Tempo + mode + dynamics map to these. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-state from music features.

concepts.name: sad_music_paradox
concepts.definition: People enjoy sad music — possibly because it offers safe emotional rehearsal + empathic engagement. Huron 2011. Substrate analogue: substrate's curiosity-drive engaging with rare emotional states without risk.

concepts.name: music_chills_neural_circuit
concepts.definition: Salimpoor + Zatorre 2011. Caudate (anticipation) + nucleus accumbens (peak pleasure) + amygdala (emotional salience). Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-circuit engaged by musical climax.

concepts.name: musical_memory
concepts.definition: Music sticks. Tip-of-the-tongue effect for melodies. Retrieval cued by music outlasts retrieval cued by lyrics. Levitin. Substrate analogue: substrate's powerful auditory event encoding.

concepts.name: earworm
concepts.definition: Involuntarily-repeating musical fragment in mind. Halpern 2009. Often catchy + repetitive. Substrate analogue: substrate's stuck-in-basin pattern with persistent activation.

concepts.name: music_and_autobiographical_memory
concepts.definition: Music strongly cues episodic memory. Songs from one's youth particularly vivid. Reminiscence bump 10-30 yrs. Janata 2009. Substrate analogue: substrate's event-binding strength for music inputs.

concepts.name: absolute_pitch
concepts.definition: Naming exact pitches without reference. Rare (~1 in 10,000); requires early exposure to musical labeling. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-pitch label association strength.

concepts.name: relative_pitch
concepts.definition: Recognizing intervals + key relationships. Trainable. Most musicians have it. Substrate analogue: substrate's relational pitch-comparison.

concepts.name: amusia
concepts.definition: Congenital inability to perceive musical pitch or rhythm — 'tone deafness'. ~4% of population. Peretz. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-domain deficit pattern.

concepts.name: infant_musicality
concepts.definition: Trehub. Infants discriminate melodies, prefer consonance over dissonance, prefer mother's singing. Universal foundation. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded musical priors before learning.

concepts.name: enculturation
concepts.definition: Cultural learning shapes which scales/rhythms are 'natural'. Western listeners predict diatonic; Indian listeners predict different. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-Mt cultural-context priors.

concepts.name: perceptual_narrowing_music
concepts.definition: Infants sensitive to all musical systems; adults best at native. Hannon + Trehub 2005. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded-Mt specialization through experience.

concepts.name: music_and_movement
concepts.definition: Music drives spontaneous movement; foot tapping, dance, head bobbing. Janata. Substrate analogue: substrate's beat-tracking driving motor reflex.

concepts.name: motor_theory_of_rhythm
concepts.definition: Rhythm perception involves motor cortex simulation. Even without actual movement. Substrate analogue: substrate's anticipatory motor pattern engagement during beat tracking.

concepts.name: rhythmic_entrainment
concepts.definition: Brain oscillations synchronise to beat. Beta + gamma in motor cortex track rhythm. Substrate analogue: substrate's clock-rate adaptation to input periodicity.

rules.name: beat_induction_extracts_pulse_from_surface
rules.head: the substrate hears rhythmic events
rules.body: it extracts the most parsimonious underlying pulse that explains the events. Large + Kolen 1994. Substrate's periodicity-extractor.

rules.name: tonal_hierarchy_drives_pitch_expectation
rules.head: the substrate processes melody in a key
rules.body: it expects next-pitch with probability matching the Krumhansl-Kessler profile for that key. Substrate's pitch-prediction prior.

rules.name: tension_resolution_drives_musical_engagement
rules.head: the substrate hears a tension-building passage
rules.body: the resolution produces a strong positive coherence-drive response. Cycle of tension-resolution sustains engagement. Substrate's drive-cycle on harmonic structure.

rules.name: expectation_violation_produces_strong_emotion
rules.head: the substrate predicts a musical continuation that is violated
rules.body: the prediction error drives surprise + emotional response. Huron's ITPRA. Substrate's high-ΔF event on music input.

rules.name: music_chills_signal_peak_anticipation_satisfaction
rules.head: the substrate anticipates a musical climax over an extended buildup
rules.body: the resolution triggers peak coherence-drive satisfaction + dopaminergic-RPE-like response. Salimpoor 2011. Substrate's reward signal on long-prediction resolution.

rules.name: rhythmic_entrainment_synchronises_oscillators
rules.head: the substrate's clock receives strong periodic input
rules.body: internal oscillators align with the input — motor cortex tracks rhythm. Substrate's tick-rate adaptation to music.
